Staffing levels have dropped, especially for nurses (although I am told this will improve next month), and this has impacted my husband physically and mentally. His medical needs are such that he requires an appointment at least once a week, but to maintain this we have been informed we have to take him into Salisbury (20 miles away), which is not possible for me, and no alternative has been offered other than to go to the MIU in Shaftesbury. This is not the standard of service expected from a practice that was rated \"Good\" by the CQC (an organization I will be contacting). Surely some contingency plans to cover basic medical needs should be in place - what has happened to patient care?\nI have lodged a formal complaint with the surgery. I was living in Broad Chalke and hadn't registered there due to the pandemic. I arrived on both occasions in a distressed state and had lost  a fair amount of blood. I asked to fill out a temporary resident form but was told to do it on line. I asked if I could do a paper copy there and then and it was with relunctance that the receptionist allowed me to complete this. I waited but was told to drive away and that a doctor would contact me. I drove down the road with my husband and the receptionist rang back.
